content.text: {"relation": "REFINED", "consensus_summary": "A disciple is a learner-follower of Jesus who obeys his teaching, imitates his life, denies self, and bears fruit; in mainstream usage it is the normative identity of every Christian (Acts equates disciples with believers), with secondary usages for the Twelve, generic adherents of any teacher, and a contested minority reading of discipleship as a higher tier of commitment.", "book_summary": "A disciple is one in whom the law is sealed and written inwardly (Isa 8:16; Jer 31:33), proven by continuing in the word, love, and fruit, and defined by the threefold 'cannot be my disciple' conditions of Luke 14 (leaving one's own, bearing the cross, forsaking all); baptized into the Name, the disciple is perfected 'as his master,' bearing the Name that carries the Word, covenant law, and priesthood (Ex 23:21; Rev 14:1).", "consensus_core_identification": "Disciple = committed learner and follower of Jesus, effectively synonymous with every genuine Christian believer.", "book_core_identification": "Disciple = a follower of Jesus in whom the covenant law is inwardly sealed, proven by the tested conditions of Luke 14 and continuance in the word, and perfected into the likeness/Name of the master.", "core_relation": "BOOK_NARROWS", "extension_relation": "BOOK_SUBSET", "boundary_disagreement": "The consensus majority treats 'disciple' as coextensive with 'believer/Christian' (Acts 6, 9, 11), entered by faith and growing lifelong. The book makes the Luke 14 'cannot' conditions and the inward sealing of the law constitutive tests: those who do not leave their own, bear the cross, and forsake all are excluded from the class of disciples even if believers. This excludes nominal or unproven believers whom the broad consensus would admit, moving toward (but with a distinctive covenantal/Name framing beyond) the minority 'higher-tier/proven disciple' alternative that Responses A, B, and C explicitly list.", "material_contradiction": "", "rationale": "The book preserves the consensus's central referent — a learner-follower of Jesus perfected as his master (Luke 6:40; John 8:31 appear in both) — so this is not replacement. But it materially tightens the boundary: discipleship is conditioned on the threefold forsaking of Luke 14 and evidenced by sealed law, continuance, love, and fruit, rather than being the default status of every baptized believer. It also adds a distinctive interpretive layer (Isa 8:16 sealing, Jer 31:33 inward law, Ex 23:21/Rev 14:1 Name-bearing) that refines rather than contradicts the consensus category. The book's own common-view note confirms it is consciously departing from the 'any believer' scope. This matches REFINED: same category, narrowed and reconditioned extension.", "citation_support": "PARTIAL", "strongest_objection": "One could argue the book's identification of the disciple as a Name-bearing, law-sealed covenant class (linking Ex 23:21 and Rev 14:1's 144,000 to discipleship) constitutes a distinctive symbolic system beyond mere narrowing, edging toward NOVEL; alternatively, since the two-tier 'proven disciple vs. mere believer' reading is already listed as a minority alternative in the consensus, one might argue it is simply covered and thus closer to MATCH with an alternative. The verdict of REFINED balances these: the referent is recognized, but the boundary and conditions are materially changed from the consensus primary.", "confidence": "high"}
